title: Nova Telecom inference cost projection and recommendations
content:
Purpose:
This working worksheet captures a before/after projection for Nova Telecom’s inference spend and latency after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. The goal is a pragmatic rollout path that hits a >35% net unit-cost reduction while preserving customer P95 latency SLAs for interactive features.

Executive summary (short):
- Current: ~USD 88k/month inference spend (hosted), dominated by real-time chat generation (81%) and embeddings for search (12%).
- Proposed Redwood Optimize changes: int8 quantization on generation models, model family switch for non-critical assistant flows, dynamic batching with 150ms batching window for low-priority requests, and prefix/KV caching for repeated session prompts.
- Projected after-optimizations: USD 47–54k/month (approx 39–47% cost reduction depending on traffic profile). Expected small tail latency increase for batched background tasks; interactive path kept under P95 280ms.

Data snapshot (input assumptions):
- Observed trailing-30d avg tokens/month (generated): 260M tokens.
- Observed trailing-30d avg prompt tokens/month (consumed): 42M tokens.
- Peak RPS observed (chat writes): 18 RPS.
- Model usage: 70% redwood-1-large (generation baseline), 20% redwood-1-small (embeddings & quick replies), 10% custom-finetuned-1 (billing/legal flows).
- Current composition of cost: 1) generation tokens 81% (compute-heavy), 2) embeddings 12%, 3) storage/IO 7%.
- Current average P95 latency (generation): 220ms; SLO target: P95 <= 300ms.

Methodology: how the numbers were derived
- Per-model per-token cost profile taken from hosted catalog pricing and recent benchmarks (internal perf matrix).
- Applied conservative perf improvements from int8 quantization (1.6x throughput uplift, ~20–30% per-token cost drop depending on sequence length).
- Dynamic batching: assume 10–18% effective cost reduction on generation when average queueing window set to 100–200ms (tradeoff measured vs P95).
- Prefix/KV caching: estimate 8–12% token reduction for multi-turn sessions with repeated system prompts (Nova’s chat reuse rate ~23%).
- Model switch (where acceptable): replace redwood-1-large for deterministic ephemeral system replies with a distilled redwood-1-med variant for 30% of calls (cheaper by ~40% per-token).
- Conservatively subtract 3–5% for implementation overhead (inefficiencies during rollout).

Before / After projection (monthly) — baseline vs recommended stack (three scenarios):
1) Conservative (safer rollout):
- Post-change spend: USD 54,200/month (~38.4% reduction)
- Key levers: int8 on non-finetuned models (50% of gen traffic), limited batching (100ms), caching pilot on top 10% sessions.
2) Mid (recommended):
- Post-change spend: USD 48,800/month (~44.5% reduction)
- Key levers: int8 across eligible models, 150ms batching for best-effort units, model switch for 30% of ephemeral replies, caching across 25% of sessions.
3) Aggressive (high risk, high reward):
- Post-change spend: USD 46,700/month (~47.0% reduction)
- Key levers: full int8/quant profiles, extended batching windows for background workers, 40% model switch, embedding quantization for search.

Breakdown example (mid scenario):
- Generation compute: from USD 71k -> USD 38k/month
- Embeddings: USD 10.5k -> USD 6.7k (quantized embeddings + caching)
- Storage/IO and misc: USD 6.5k -> USD 4.1k
- Net monthly savings: USD 39.2k

Latency and UX impact (risks):
- Interactive P95: target kept under 300ms by routing low-latency requests to unbatched priority pool. Minor added tail variance (+10–30ms) expected for int8 inlined paths.
- Batched best-effort requests: can see P95 increase 120–250ms depending on window; acceptable for async jobs (SMS digest generation, scheduled reports).
- Model quality risk: switching to distilled variants can introduce subtle changes in tone/completion length. Recommend A/B testing and a human eval set of ~1k prompts before broad rollout.

Implementation roadmap (quarter view):
- Week 1–2: Kickoff, confirm list of eligible models and traffic routing rules. Owners: Priya (product), Marco (infra).
- Week 3–5: Build and test quant profiles in staging (int8, int4 sanity runs). Owner: Marco.
- Week 6–7: Canary rollout for prefix caching (10% sessions), collect hit-rate and correctness metrics. Owner: Selene.
- Week 8–9: Enable dynamic batching for non-priority routes (150ms window), observe latency/cost delta. Owner: Marco.
- Week 10: Model switch for ephemeral replies behind canary (5% -> 20% -> 30%). Owner: Priya.
- Week 11–12: Roll to 75% with monitoring checks, ramp to 100% if metrics stable.

Estimated engineering effort and dependencies:
- Infra changes: batching controller + routing policies (2 engineers x 4 weeks or 1.5 FTE-month)
- Serving/runtime tuning: quant profile validation + perf benchmarking (1 engineer x 3 weeks)
- Product/QA: eval and content checks (0.5 FTE x 6 weeks)
- Total approx: 2.5–3.0 engineering FTE-months (concurrent work).
- Dependencies: access to Nova's test prompts, feature-flagging infra, canary routing in console.

Monitoring and acceptance criteria:
- Cost: verified drop in per-1M generated tokens cost to <= USD 165 (mid scenario target) within 30 days of full rollout.
- Quality: human-eval threshold: <3% regression on top-1 relevance metrics and no more than 5% drop on customer satisfaction samples.
- Latency: interactive P95 <= 300ms sustained during peak hours for three consecutive 7-day windows.
- Stability: error rate for generation endpoints remains <0.2% and similar to baseline.

Rollback and mitigation plan:
- Feature flags: everything behind flags with instant rollback to baseline model/profile.
- Capacity fallback: route to dedicated (non-quantized) pool automatically if error rates spike or quality regression crosses threshold.
- Observability: prebuilt dashboards for cost, P95, error rate, human-eval delta, and prefix cache hit rate.

Next steps / asks from Nova Telecom:
- Provide anonymized 30-day prompt sample (1k–3k sessions) and usage tags for session-types (billing, support, marketing).
- Approve limited model-switch A/B tests on ephemeral replies.
- Confirm priority routes that must never be batched (billing confirmation, 2FA messaging).

Appendix: quick spreadsheet layout (for the shared sheet linked above)
- Tabs: raw-usage, per-model-cost, scenario-matrix, rollout-tasks, evaluation-summaries
- Key columns (per-model-cost): model, baseline-per-token, post-quant-per-token, typical-seq-len, monthly-tokens, baseline-cost, post-cost, delta, notes
- Scenario-matrix rows: conservative / mid / aggressive with explicit assumptions pull-downs to attach to rows

Notes and open questions (working):
- Need to confirm contract terms for dedicated capacity if routing falls back; it may alter ROI calculus.
- Investigate whether embedding cache TTLs can be tuned for telecom search use-cases without stale results.
- Check legal on switching finetuned model variants for sensitive flows.

Status: this doc is a working projection and recommendation set. Numbers are draft — linked sheet contains the calculator and raw inputs. Please review and mark items needing more conservative assumptions before exec presentation.
summary: Working before/after cost projection for Nova Telecom showing 39–47% potential reduction through quantization, batching, caching, and selective model-swap; roadmap and monitoring included.
